summary: Joshua gathers tribes at Shechem, recites history: Terah beyond River served other gods, I took Abraham, multiplied, gave Isaac, Jacob and Esau, sent Moses and Aaron, plagues in Egypt, brought out through sea, gave Amorite land, Balak and Balaam, you did not fight, you eat vineyards you did not plant. Now therefore fear Yahweh, serve in sincerity and truth, put away gods fathers served beyond River and Egypt, choose today whom you will serve, whether gods beyond River or Amorites, but as for me and my house we will serve Yahweh. People say we will serve, Joshua says you cannot, you are witnesses against yourselves, put away foreign gods, they do, Joshua makes covenant, writes in book of law, sets up large stone under oak as witness, says stone heard all words, will be witness.
whyItMatters: Climax of Joshua — Shechem covenant renewal echoing Exodus call. Most quoted 'as for me and my house we will serve Yahweh.' Shows choice, history, witness stone.

context.author: Joshua trad

keyVerses.text: If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.”
keyVerses.why: Central choice — personal and household decision.

keyVerses.text: I gave you a land on which you had not labored, and cities which you didn’t build, and you live in them. You eat of vineyards and olive groves which you didn’t plant.’
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he took a great stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of Yahweh.
keyVerses.why: Stone as witness — creation hears covenant.

questions.question: Why recite entire history from Terah to present?
questions.answer: Covenant renewal pattern: Suzerain recounts benevolent acts before asking loyalty — I brought you out, gave land you didn't labor, cities, vineyards. History shows grace before law — you eat what you didn't plant. Choosing is response to story, not abstract rule. Shechem is where Abraham first received promise and Jacob buried idols — full circle.

questions.question: What does 'choose today whom you will serve' mean? Isn't they must serve Yahweh?
questions.answer: Joshua offers real choice: gods beyond River (Terah's gods, Mesopotamian), gods of Egypt (where you were), gods of Amorites (current land), or Yahweh. Choice is not between equally good options but between rival allegiances present in community. 'Me and my house we will serve Yahweh' is personal and household decision, not just individual. Most quoted verse for family dedication.

questions.question: Why does Joshua say 'You cannot serve Yahweh, he is holy, jealous'? Sounds discouraging.
questions.answer: After people quickly say we will serve, Joshua pushes back: you cannot (in own strength), he is holy and jealous, will not forgive transgression if you forsake and serve foreign gods, will turn and do you harm after doing you good. Sobering realism — covenant with holy God is serious, not casual. He wants counted cost, not easy promise. They insist, so he says you are witnesses against yourselves, then commands put away foreign gods that are among you — revealing idols still present despite verbal commitment.

glossary.def: Covenant renewal site — Abraham first altar, Jacob buried idols, Joshua renewal, later kingdom divided.
Decision point — rival allegiances still present, requires daily choosing.
Creation hears covenant — stone under oak as enduring witness.
